Commentary.Commentary: Kusal Perera sparkled with a brilliant 110 while Tharanga remained unbeaten 110, albeit it was a slow one. Silva and Karunaratne were cautious while Mendis was carefree. de Silva and Perera could have done better but Gunaratne impressed. Stay tuned for the second innings.

Sri Lanka will be pleased with their batting display, with the only complaint being that of only two batsmen getting centuries while four could not convert their starts. Still, they will be pleased as a unit and will hope that their bowling gets 3-4 wickets by the end of the day.

A handy achievement for Zimbabwe, considering that they managed to pick up 10 Sri Lankan wickets. The skipper led from the front, with Graeme Cremer taking 4 wickets while Mpofu got 2 at the end. But things could have been better had they taken their chances.

It was all Sri Lanka yesterday as first, the openers put up a good and solid platform before Kusal Perera attacked the hosts into oblivion. Zimbabwe did get some things going their way, as they managed to pick up 4 wickets. Can they get the remaining 6 quickly today? Or will we see the Lankans pile on a huge first innings total? Hello and a warm welcome to the second day's play of the first Test between Zimbabwe and Sri Lanka in Harare.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

That is it from us then! Can Zimbabwe make this second new ball talk tomorrow? The partnership between Tharanga and de Silva is still young and if they can break that quickly, they can run into an inexperienced middle and lower order. Join us at 1330 IST (0800 GMT) for the second day's play. Adios! Take Care!

Zimbabwe have to blame themselves for this poor day. They missed as many as 5 chances and gave plenty of let-offs to the batsmen. Had those been taken, the situation would have been much more competitive. The seamers bowled their heart out on a surface which has nothing much to offer but skipper Graeme Cremer picked up 3 wickets.

Kaushal Silva was unlucky to miss out on a century but Kusal Perera was the one who changed the tempo of the innings. His 110 from 121 balls took Zimbabwe by storm and pegged them back. In the final session, the Lankans did lose some wickets but they had the match in control.

End of an excellent day for the Lankans. They got it right from the toss and then scored the runs, taking full advantage of a flat track. The openers were slow but then the middle order started to score quickly.

TOSS - Time for the toss. Graeme Cremer tosses the coin, heads is the call from Rangana Herath and it is a head. SRI LANKA WILL BAT.
PITCH REPORT - The track looks a good one to bat upon. There are a few cracks which might widen as the days progress. That will make batting difficult as the game goes on.
WEATHER REPORT - It is a perfect day for cricket with outstanding weather. Just a little bit of breeze blowing across and not that hot.

We are all in readiness for Sri Lanka's tour of Zimbabwe. They will play two Tests, followed by a tri-series, involving the West Indies, later in November. Big day for the hosts, as they are playing their 100th Test. Can they perform with something to cherish?
